story:
A giant king ruled over an island realm. He was brother to a woman, and to several half-brothers, one of whom was prone to violent jealousy. A foreign king sailed with thirteen ships to ask for the king's sister in marriage, seeking an alliance between the two lands. The giant king agreed, and a wedding feast was held in tents, since no house could hold his massive body. Furious that he had not been consulted, the jealous half-brother mutilated all the foreign king's horses. To make amends, the giant king gave the offended king a magic cauldron that could restore the dead to life, though the revived could not speak. Pleased, the foreign king sailed home with his new wife.

The wife bore a son, but resentment over the maimed horses lingered, and the foreign court forced her into the kitchen, where she was abused for three years. She tamed a bird and sent it with a message to her brother, who declared war. He waded across the sea himself, since no ship could bear him, while his army sailed behind. When the enemy blocked a river crossing, the giant king lay down his own body as a bridge for his troops. The enemy, seeming to yield, offered his nephew the kingship and built a great house to host the giant, but hid a hundred armed men in flour-sacks to ambush the feast. The suspicious half-brother crushed the skulls of the hidden men. At the feast he also flung his sister's young son into the fire, sparking battle. The enemy revived their dead with the magic cauldron until the half-brother hid among the corpses and let himself be thrown in, shattering the cauldron and dying in the act. The giant king was mortally wounded in the foot. He ordered his men to cut off his head and carry it to be buried facing the enemy's homeland to ward off invasion. The survivors feasted with the still-speaking head for years before completing the burial. The sister, grieving, died of a broken heart.
